# Mahāsudassanacariya (Cp 4)
**ID:** Cp 4
**Section:** Cariyāpiṭaka (cp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1

**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/cp4

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
According to DharmaNexus text-reuse data, the *Mahāsudassanacariya* shares three passages with the seventh volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, with its longest shared match occurring between segments §2.4–4.4 and §2150–2154 [DharmaNexus]. The text is also noted on SuttaCentral in connection with the *Mahānāradakassapajātaka* (Ja 545) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus additionally records six automatic cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā* (D3790), though these represent machine-detected formulaic reuses rather than direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in (SuttaCentral): Ja 545 Mahānāradakassapajātaka
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Sattamo bhāgo) (Atk S0514a3) (§2.4–4.4 ↔ §2150–2154)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཉི་ཤུ་ལྔ་པ། (pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā) (D3790) [bo]
**Sources**

- [SuttaCentral] SuttaCentral entry for cp4 (Mahāsudassanacariya) — Supplied canonical metadata, English title, translation listings, and cross-reference to Ja 545.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus database matches for PA_cp_4 — Provided automated textual reuse data for Pali-internal matches with Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā and cross-language alignments with Tibetan D3790.
- [Bareau] André Bareau, 'Les récits canoniques du Cariyāpiṭaka et les Jātaka Pāli' — Attested the title and position as the fourth narrative of the Cariyāpiṭaka, and its nature as an abridged Bodhisatta narrative.
- [Matsumura 1980] Hisashi Matsumura, Four Avadānas from the Gilgit Manuscripts (1980) — Contextualized Cp I.4 among parallel versions of the Mahāsudassana story (DN 17, Turfan Sanskrit manuscripts) and noted the commentary Paramatthadīpanī.
